messages:
maria: Quick thread — Q3 hosted API capacity plan draft. proposal: buy-to-cover baseline demand, short-term lease slices for predictable seasonal spikes, plus a regional holdback (safety pool) to absorb zone/regional failures. sharing numbers and open to pushback.

sam: sounds reasonable. what baseline are you sizing off?

maria: baseline = 420 steady-serving GPUs across EU+NA (this is after current reserved capacity), with 8% expected organic growth q/q. that converts to ~12.7k GPU-hours/week baseline.

jia: can you break that into burst vs steady? we need to know how much we expect to hit autoscale vs leased burst.

maria: yes — expected steady 420, expected burst windows add ~120 GPUs for 1–3 weeks (holiday promo / partner test windows). planning an optional lease tranche of 200 GPUs in two 6-week blocks we can spin up in region-specific pools.

lucas: cost check — ballpark lease cost is $0.55/hr/GPU for the vendors we vetted, purchase amortized is ~$0.22/hr/GPU (3yr). do we have preference to prefer buy for NA and lease for APAC/EU to avoid shipping delays?

sam: agree — prefer buy for NA where lead times are shortest. EU should be mixed (buy for core, lease for surge), APAC lean on leases where wholesale availability is flaky.

anya: network question — adding 200 GPUs in a region will need extra TORs and transits; we hit port density limits last quarter in eu-west-1 during a burst test. do we have rack / switch headroom tracked?

maria: noted. ops-infra inventory shows ~15% spare port capacity in eu-west-1 but only 6% in ap-southeast-1. plan to reserve a small cabling budget for eu-west, and prefer leases for ap-southeast.

ops-bot: Deploy alert: scheduled lease-test deployment window reserved for 2026-07-10..2026-08-21. Use tag #lease-tranche-test.

jia: can we quantify GPU-hours required for the lease tranche? I want to compare cost/benefit versus overprovisioning buys.

maria: quick calc (approx):
```
lease_tranche = 200 GPUs * 6 weeks * 7 days * 24 hrs = 200 * 1008 = 201,600 GPU-hours per tranche
cost_lease_tranche = 201,600 * $0.55 = $110,880
buy_equivalent_hours_3yr = 200 * 3*52*7*24 = 200 * 26280 = 5,256,000 GPU-hours amortized
amortized_monthly_cost_buy = (5,256,000 * $0.22) / 36 months ≈ $32,189/mo (per 200 GPUs)
```
Numbers fuzzy but useful for tradeoff.

lucas: thanks. also factor in opportunity cost — buys are long tail but reduce unit costs; leases let us avoid cold start waste.

sam: recommendation: buy 120 GPUs for NA this quarter (adds to baseline), mix-buy 60 GPUs for EU, and hold two lease tranches of 200 GPUs each to be used cross-region as needed. also keep 10% regional holdback (by instance) as hot spare.

anya: operational ask: before we commit buys, we need to confirm TOR port refresh in eu-west (rack order lead 4–6 weeks) and get network budget approved. putting a cal request in.

maria: I'll open a CAPEX request for the buys and a purchase-order for the lease vendors. also attaching rollout plan for canarying capacity increments and automated health checks.

jia: add a graceful-degrade policy to prefer smaller model variants in a region when burst is saturated. reduces GPU demand per token.

maria: noted — add to rollout runbook: canary 10% traffic to new capacity, monitor token latency and tail p99, fallback to canary region if packet loss >1%.

ops-bot: Runbook created: https://c.ops/redwood/runbooks/q3-capacity-holdback (created by maria)

lucas: timeline checks out. target order placement week of 2026-06-14 to meet Q3 ingress. any objections?

sam: none from me.

anya: approve pending network budget sign-off.

maria: ok. I'll circulate the CAPEX + procurement plan and schedule a 20min sync tomorrow to lock numbers. thanks all :thumbsup:
